    • Hitachi Projector

    Written on December 14, 2023

    By Analicia Abernathy

    Started a new teardown today, a Hitachi Projector Model CP-X2521WN that I got a few months back. Was fun, not overly challenging to do, lots of neat colored glass and lens were found. Of course metal as always is going off for recycling to my local yard, plastic with standard recycling and boards will be depopulated and sold for scrap as well.

    To start off I removed the screws from the bottom along the border (fig. 1) and a few of the screws off the rear connections panel (fig. 2). This allowed me to flip it back to right side up and lift the top straight off (fig. 3).

    With the cover removed I could now see the insides of the machine (fig. 4), which was pretty fun to gaze upon as it was. From here I could plan what to remove next. I unplugged and unscrewed as many wires as I could from the main board then removed the housing that contained the light (fig. 5). I don't have additional images but it was the projector light bulb in its plastic housing. Nothing much but a few power wires to remove and add to my copper wire pile.

    From there I removed the screws that held down the main board and took that off (fig. 6). It will go into my bucket off boards that I need to depopulate the components off of at a later date. But here is a few close ups of the board itself (fig. 7 and fig. 8) and the connections for different equipment as well (fig. 9). With the main board out of the way I moved on to one of the 2 cooling systems. On the bottom left I removed the large black shielding and the fans that fit under neat below the lamp housing. This as well exposed another smaller control board, in this case what I believe is the main power distribution board (fig. 6).

    Unclipping the wires and removing the screws from the power board I was able to lift that out of place.
